lines: No workstation means I notice things. People underestimate the unemployed at their own <bold>peril</bold>.
Some jobs use tools. Mine seems to be hearing every <wavy>rumor</wavy> before lunch.
I am between callings, which is a polite way to say the village has not decided what to <shake>blame</shake> me for yet.
Everyone asks what I do. I ask why they are all in such a <jump>hurry</jump>.
A workstation gives you a job. Not having one gives you a view of <italic>everyone else's</italic>.
I may not have a profession, but I have <bold>opinions</bold>, and somehow those take up more time.
People with jobs are always busy. People without jobs are always being <pulse>watched</pulse>.
I am not idle. I am <italic>observing inefficiently</italic>.
The village keeps waiting for me to become useful. I keep waiting for the village to lower its <shake>standards</shake>.
No tools, no counter, no schedule. Just me, the street, and a <wavy>suspicious</wavy> amount of free time.
I help where I can and avoid jobs that begin with shouting.
Someone has to notice when every workstation is busy.
I know a little about most trades and enough to stay out of the way.
The village keeps offering advice instead of employment.
I have time to listen, which is why nobody can keep a secret from me.
My schedule is open. My enthusiasm depends on the task.
I am considering several careers and rejecting them carefully.
Today I carried water, found a lost chicken, and remained unpaid.
Not having a trade means every chore can find me.
I may lack a workstation, but I never lack an opinion.
People are talking about you differently. I am <bold>very</bold> good at hearing that sort of thing.
Something <pulse>shifted</pulse>. Same street, different looks.
You changed the village's mind a little. That is harder than moving a <shake>bed</shake>.
The way people glance at you is different now. I notice <italic>glances</italic>. I have time.
Your name came up today, and nobody said it the <wavy>usual way</wavy>.
The village has adjusted its opinion. Villages do that <pulse>slowly</pulse>, then all at once.
I do not know what you did, but the air around your name has <pulse>changed</pulse>.
People are either <color:green>softer</color> about you or <color:red>sharper</color>. Hard to tell yet, but it is not the same.
You should know the <wavy>gossip</wavy> moved. I followed it for a while.
Around here, reputation changes one <italic>whispered sentence</italic> at a time.
More people wave when you pass now. Or fewer. You probably noticed.
Someone defended your name at the well today.
The village remembers what you did, even if I forgot the details.
Doors open faster for people the village likes.
I heard three stories about you, and two were almost the same.
Folks watch you less closely than they used to. That seems good.
You get a different kind of silence in the square now.
People made up their minds about you while pretending not to.
Your name sounds better in conversation lately.
Whatever you did changed how everyone looks at you.
